335316.title: Double-exponential lower bound conjecture for r_4(5,n)

full_literal_record.title: Double-exponential lower bound conjecture for r_4(5,n)
full_literal_record.statement:
Let $r_4(5,n)$ be the off-diagonal Ramsey number for 4-uniform hypergraphs, the least $N$ such that every red-blue coloring of the 4-edges of an $N$-vertex complete hypergraph contains a red copy of the complete 4-uniform hypergraph on 5 vertices or a blue copy on $n$ vertices. **The $r_4(5,n)$ lower-bound conjecture.** For $n\geq 5$, there is an absolute constant $c>0$ such that

$$
r_4(5,n)>2^{2^{n^c}}.
$$

The conjecture would improve the best known lower bound for $r_4(5,n)$ from a single exponential of the form $2^{n^{c\log\log n}}$ to a double exponential. The source notes that this conjecture follows from the crucial diagonal conjecture for $r_3(n,n)$ established earlier in the paper's discussion, but it remains unproved here.
full_literal_record.source_name: Dhruv Mubayi and Andrew Suk, “New lower bounds for hypergraph Ramsey numbers”, arXiv:1702.05509 (2018).
full_literal_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.05509

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2017).

324773.title: Off-diagonal semi-algebraic Ramsey bound

full_literal_record.title: Off-diagonal semi-algebraic Ramsey bound
full_literal_record.statement:
For integers $k\geq 3$, dimension $d$, complexity $t$, and $s$, let $R_k^{d,t}(s,n)$ be the least integer $N$ such that every sequence of $N$ points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ and every $k$-ary semi-algebraic relation of complexity at most $t$ contains either $s$ points all of whose induced $k$-tuples belong to the relation or $n$ points none of whose induced $k$-tuples belong to it. **Off-diagonal semi-algebraic Ramsey conjecture.** For fixed $k\geq 3,d,t$, and $s$, there is a constant $c=c(k,d,t,s)$ such that

$$
R_k^{d,t}(s,n)\leq \operatorname{twr}_{k-2}(n^c).
$$

This would improve the general tower-height upper bound by one level in the off-diagonal case. The paper presents it as a stronger expected bound, with the crucial $k=3$ case conjectured separately in polynomial form.
full_literal_record.source_name: David Conlon, Jacob Fox, János Pach, Benny Sudakov and Andrew Suk, “Ramsey-type results for semi-algebraic relations”, arXiv:1301.0074 (2013).
full_literal_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1301.0074

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2013).

321860.title: The secretary problem bound for posets with a fixed number of maximal elements

full_literal_record.title: The secretary problem bound for posets with a fixed number of maximal elements
full_literal_record.statement:
Let $(P,\prec)$ be a poset with $k$ maximal elements. Define

$$
p_k=\begin{cases}\frac{1}{e},&k=1,\\[0.3ex]\sqrt[k-1]{\frac{1}{k}},&k>1.\end{cases}
$$

**Secretary problem conjecture.** There is an algorithm for the secretary problem on $(P,\prec)$ that is successful with probability at least $p_k$.

The bound is proved in the source for posets of width $k$ and is expected to extend to all posets with $k$ maximal elements; it is not known from the supplied text whether the same algorithm works universally or another algorithm depending only on $k$ is required.
full_literal_record.source_name: Bryn Garrod and Robert Morris, “The secretary problem on an unknown poset”, arXiv:1107.1379 (2012).
full_literal_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1107.1379

358545.title: Large trees dominate even paths in the homomorphism-density order

full_literal_record.title: Large trees dominate even paths in the homomorphism-density order
full_literal_record.statement:
For non-empty graphs $H$ and $T$, write $H\succcurlyeq T$ when

$$
t(H,G)^{e(T)}\geq t(T,G)^{e(H)}
$$

for every graph $G$. Let $P_{2k}$ denote the path with $2k$ vertices.

**Large-tree path conjecture.** For every $k\geq 1$, there exists an integer $n_0(k)$ such that every tree $H$ with at least $n_0(k)$ vertices satisfies

$$
H\succcurlyeq P_{2k}.
$$

The statement is proposed as a weaker generalization motivated by the partial order on trees; the source gives no resolution, so it remains open.

365375.title: Odd-length linear equations are uncommon over the integers

full_literal_record.title: Odd-length linear equations are uncommon over the integers
full_literal_record.statement:
Let $k\geq 3$ be odd, and let $a_1,\ldots,a_k\in\mathbb{Z}\setminus\{0\}$. Consider the equation

$$
a_1x_1+\cdots+a_kx_k=0.
$$

Call the equation **uncommon** over the integers when there is a 2-coloring of $[n]$ with fewer monochromatic solutions than a uniformly random 2-coloring.

358120.title: Esperet–Lemoine–Maffray conjecture on induced paths in degenerate graphs

full_literal_record.title: Esperet–Lemoine–Maffray conjecture on induced paths in degenerate graphs
full_literal_record.statement:
Let $k\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $G$ be a $k$-degenerate graph with a path of order $n\geq 1$. An **induced path** is a path whose vertices induce exactly the edges of the path in $G$. **Esperet–Lemoine–Maffray's conjecture.** For every $k\in\mathbb{N}$ there is a constant $c>0$ such that $G$ has an induced path of order at least

$$
(\log n)^c.
$$

This conjecture asks for a polylogarithmic lower bound on the order of an induced path in every bounded-degeneracy graph containing a path of order $n$. The known general lower bound is of order $\log\log n$, while planar graphs and more generally graphs of bounded Euler genus satisfy stronger polylogarithmic bounds; the conjecture remains open in the stated generality.
full_literal_record.source_name: Oscar Defrain and Jean-Florent Raymond, “Sparse graphs without long induced paths”, arXiv:2304.09679 (2023).
full_literal_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.09679

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2023).

360893.title: Norine–Thomas linear-density conjecture for degree-three vertices in minimal bricks

full_literal_record.title: Norine–Thomas linear-density conjecture for degree-three vertices in minimal bricks
full_literal_record.statement:
A **brick** is a 3-connected bicritical graph. A brick $G$ is **minimal** if $G-e$ is not a brick for every edge $e$ of $G$. Write $V(G)$ for its vertex set and let $|V(G)|$ denote the number of vertices.

318597.title: A single covariance sign change in random orientations of $G(n,m)$

full_literal_record.title: A single covariance sign change in random orientations of $G(n,m)$
full_literal_record.statement:
Let $G(n,m)$ be the uniformly random graph with exactly $m$ edges on $n$ vertices, and orient every present edge independently and uniformly at random. Fix distinct vertices $s,a,b$, and let $A$ be the event that there is no directed path from $a$ to $s$, while $B$ is the event that there is no directed path from $s$ to $b$. The covariance in question is

$$
\operatorname{Cov}(\mathbf{1}_A,\mathbf{1}_B)=\mathbb{P}(A\cap B)-\mathbb{P}(A)\mathbb{P}(B).
$$

**Single-sign-change conjecture.** For any fixed $n\ge 5$, the covariance in $G(n,m)$ changes sign only once between two values of $m$.
full_literal_record.source_name: Sven Erick Alm, Svante Janson and Svante Linusson, “Correlations for paths in random orientations of G(n,p) and G(n,m)”, arXiv:0906.0720 (2010).

324970.title: Kohayakawa–Łuczak–Rödl sparse embedding conjecture

full_literal_record.title: Kohayakawa–Łuczak–Rödl sparse embedding conjecture
full_literal_record.statement:
Let $\alpha>0$, $d>0$, and let $F$ be a graph with vertex set $V(F)=[\ell]$. For $p\in(0,1]$ and integers $m,M$, let $\mathcal G(F,m,M,\varepsilon,p,d)$ be the family of balanced $\ell$-partite graphs whose relevant pairs are $(\varepsilon,p)$-regular and each have exactly $M\geq dpm^2$ edges. Let $\mathcal B(F,m,M,\varepsilon,p,d)$ be the subfamily containing no partite copy of $F$, and let $m_2(F)$ be the $2$-density of $F$. **Kohayakawa–Łuczak–Rödl conjecture.** There exist $\varepsilon>0$, $C>0$, and $m_0$ such that, for every $m\geq m_0$, $p\geq Cm^{-1/m_2(F)}$, and $M\geq dpm^2$,

$$
|\mathcal B(F,m,M,\varepsilon,p,d)|\leq \alpha^M|\mathcal G(F,m,M,\varepsilon,p,d)|.
$$

The conjecture was verified for 2-balanced graphs by Balogh, Morris and Samotij and for all graphs by Saxton and Thomason, so it is solved.
full_literal_record.source_name: Vojtěch Rödl and Mathias Schacht, “Extremal results in random graphs”, arXiv:1302.2248 (2013).
full_literal_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1302.2248

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of February 2013); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

319471.title: A uniform cut-product bound for random Fibonacci words

full_literal_record.title: A uniform cut-product bound for random Fibonacci words
full_literal_record.statement:
Let $A_n$ be the set of random Fibonacci words of order $n$, let $f_n$ denote their length, and let $A_n[i,j]$ denote the set of subwords occurring in positions $i$ through $j$. Define

$$
c_n=\frac{}{}\max_{1\leq k\leq f_n-1}\frac{\big|A_n[1,k]\big|\cdot\big|A_n[k+1,f_n]\big|}{|A_n|}.
$$

**Uniform cut-product conjecture.** There is a constant $C$ such that for all $n\geq 3$ and $1\leq k\leq f_n-1$,

$$
\big|A_n[1,k]\big|\cdot\big|A_n[k+1,f_n]\big|\leq C\cdot |A_n|.
$$

The conjecture asserts that the number of ways to choose the two parts of a random Fibonacci word across any cut is uniformly bounded by a constant multiple of the total number of random Fibonacci words. It is motivated by computer calculations, while the supplied source does not establish whether the conjecture has been resolved.
full_literal_record.source_name: Johan Nilsson, “On the Entropy of Random Fibonacci Words”, arXiv:1001.3513 (2010).

363222.title: Liu–Montgomery's crux conjecture for clique subdivisions

full_literal_record.title: Liu–Montgomery's crux conjecture for clique subdivisions
full_literal_record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph and let $calpha=\tfrac{1}{100}$. For a subgraph $H\subset G$, write $d(H)$ for its average degree, and let $C_{\alpha}(G)$ be the minimum order of a subgraph $H\subset G$ with $d(H)\geq \alpha d(G)$. A **subdivision** of a clique is obtained by replacing each edge of the clique by internally vertex-disjoint paths.

**Liu–Montgomery's crux conjecture.** There exists some constant $c>0$ such that every graph $G$ contains a subdivision of a clique with at least

$$
c\min \Big\{d(G), \sqrt{\tfrac{C_{\alpha}(G)}{\log C_{\alpha}(G)}}\Big\}
$$

vertices.

The conjecture formalizes the idea that graphs without a small subgraph almost as dense as the whole graph should contain a large clique subdivision. The parameter $C_{\alpha}(G)$ is the crux, measuring the order of the smallest dense patch; the source states that Liu and Montgomery raised this conjecture with $\alpha=\tfrac{1}{100}$, but gives no resolution here.
full_literal_record.source_name: Donglei Yang and Fan Yang, “Embedding clique subdivisions via crux”, arXiv:2405.15409 (2024).
full_literal_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.15409

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2024).

full_literal_record.title: Small $K_5$-models at average degree greater than six
full_literal_record.statement:

379626.title: Narayana polynomials form a q-log-convex sequence

full_literal_record.title: Narayana polynomials form a q-log-convex sequence
full_literal_record.statement: The Narayana number $N(n,k)$ counts Dyck paths of length $2n$ with exactly $k$ peaks, and the Narayana polynomials are $N_n(q)=\sum_{k=0}^{n}N(n,k)q^k$. A sequence of polynomials is **q-log-convex** when each difference $N_{n+1}(q)N_{n-1}(q)-N_n(q)^2$ has nonnegative coefficients. **Narayana polynomials conjecture.** The Narayana polynomials $N_n(q)$ form a $q$-log-convex sequence. This was verified for $n\leq 100$ using Maple; pointwise log-convexity for each fixed nonnegative $q$ is known, but coefficientwise $q$-log-convexity remains the conjectural strengthening.
full_literal_record.source_name: Li Liu and Yi Wang, “On the log-convexity of combinatorial sequences”, arXiv:math/0602672 (2006).

362298.title: Fox–Sudakov polynomial Rödl conjecture

full_literal_record.title: Fox–Sudakov polynomial Rödl conjecture
full_literal_record.statement:
Let $H$ be a graph. For a graph $G$, a vertex set $S$ is **$\varepsilon$-homogeneous** if the edge density of the induced graph $G[S]$ is at most $\varepsilon$ or at least $1-\varepsilon$.

**Fox–Sudakov's conjecture.** For any graph $H$ there exists a $C_H>0$ such that for any $0<\varepsilon \le 1/2$ any $n$-vertex $H$-free graph contains an $\varepsilon$-homogeneous set with at least $\varepsilon^{C_H}n$ vertices.

This is a polynomial quantitative strengthening of Rödl's theorem and implies the Erdős–Hajnal conjecture for each fixed graph $H$. The source presents it as an open conjecture, while the paper proves equivalence with the Erdős–Hajnal and polynomial Nikiforov conjectures.

353682.title: Conjecture on the giant d-rigid component and its double core

full_literal_record.title: Conjecture on the giant d-rigid component and its double core
full_literal_record.statement:
Let $d\ge 2$, $c>0$, and let $G\sim\mathcal G(n,c/n)$. A **$d$-rigid component** is an inclusion-maximal $d$-rigid induced subgraph of positive density. Let $C$ be the $(d+1)$-core of $G$. The **$((d+1)+d)$-core** $\widehat C$ is obtained from $C$ by repeatedly adding, as long as possible, a vertex with at least $d$ neighbors in the current vertex set.

**Giant $d$-rigid component conjecture.** Then a.a.s.:

- if $c<c_d$, there is no $d$-rigid component in $G$ with more than $3$ vertices;
- if $c>c_d$, $G$ contains a unique $d$-rigid component of positive density, consisting of the vertices of its $((d+1)+d)$-core.

This gives the conjectured sharp transition from the absence of nontrivial large rigid components to a unique giant component, and identifies the giant through the iterated core construction. The threshold is related to the known threshold for $d$-orientability, while the rigidity assertions remain open.
full_literal_record.source_name: Alan Lew, Eran Nevo, Yuval Peled and Orit E. Raz, “Sharp threshold for rigidity of random graphs”, arXiv:2202.09917 (2022).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.09917

347848.title: The random-regular-graph MaxCut pseudoexpectation conjecture

full_literal_record.title: The random-regular-graph MaxCut pseudoexpectation conjecture
full_literal_record.statement:
Let $d\geq 3$, and let $G$ be a random $d$-regular graph on $n$ vertices. A **pseudoexpectation operator** $\widetilde{\mathop{\varmathbb{E}}}$ of degree $n^\delta$ is the degree-bounded SoS relaxation used in the source, acting on Boolean variables $x_i$.

**Random-regular-graph MaxCut conjecture.** For some $\delta>0$, with high probability there is a degree-$n^\delta$ pseudoexpectation operator $\widetilde{\mathop{\varmathbb{E}}}$ on Boolean variables $x_i$ whose MaxCut value is at least

$$
\frac{1}{2}+\frac{\sqrt{d-1}}{d}\bigl(1-\operatorname{o}_{d,n}(1)\bigr).
$$

This conjecture concerns the MaxCut setting arising from the proposed planted-problem extension to bottom eigenspaces of random adjacency matrices. It asserts that a low-degree SoS relaxation can certify a value at least the displayed spectral-threshold expression; the source supplies no resolution.

348006.title: The monotonicity conjecture for polychromatic 2-regular subgraphs

full_literal_record.title: The monotonicity conjecture for polychromatic 2-regular subgraphs
full_literal_record.statement:
Let $K_n$ be the complete graph on $n$ vertices. A subgraph is **2-regular** if every vertex has degree $2$. An edge-coloring of $K_n$ is called polychromatic for a family of subgraphs when every subgraph in the family receives all colors used by the coloring.

**Monotonicity conjecture.** Let $n\geq 6$ and let $j$ be an integer such that $3\leq j<n$; if $j=5$, assume $n\geq 9$. If an edge-coloring $\varphi$ of $K_n$ has the property that every 2-regular subgraph spanning $j$ vertices gets all colors, then every 2-regular subgraph spanning at least $j$ vertices gets all colors under $\varphi$.

The conjecture extends the authors' results for cycles to 2-regular graphs. It is presented as an expected analogue of a proved cycle theorem, with possible exceptions only in small cases; the supplied text gives no resolution.
full_literal_record.source_name: John Goldwasser and Ryan Hansen, “Polychromatic colorings of 1-regular and 2-regular subgraphs of complete graphs”, arXiv:2009.08960 (2020).

372165.title: Linear zero-sum Ramsey bound for graphs of bounded degeneracy

full_literal_record.title: Linear zero-sum Ramsey bound for graphs of bounded degeneracy
full_literal_record.statement:
Let $d\geq 2$ be an integer. For a graph $G$, write $R(G,\Gamma_0)$ for its zero-sum Ramsey number with respect to a finite abelian group $\Gamma_0$, and let $n=e(G)$ be the number of edges of $G$. **Bounded-degeneracy conjecture.** There exists a constant $C=C(d)$ such that, for every graph $G$ with degeneracy at most $d$ and every finite abelian group $\Gamma_0$ whose order divides $n$, one has

$$
R(G,\Gamma_0)\leq C\cdot n.
$$

The paper proves a linear zero-sum Ramsey bound for bounded-degree graphs and notes that the analogous statement for graphs of bounded degeneracy is expected, motivated by the known linear classical Ramsey bound for this family. The conjectured extension is not proved here.
full_literal_record.source_name: Jasmin Katz, Xiaopan Lian, Alexandru Malekshahian and Andrey Shapiro, “A linear upper bound for zero-sum Ramsey numbers of bounded degree graphs”, arXiv:2512.17790 (2026).

366912.title: Pointwise Weyl-law improvement for selected surfaces of revolution

full_literal_record.title: Pointwise Weyl-law improvement for selected surfaces of revolution
full_literal_record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{S}\in\mathfrak{S}$, and let $K_\varepsilon$ be the set of points of $\mathcal{S}$ at distance at least $\varepsilon$ from both poles. Let $N(\lambda,x)$ denote the pointwise eigenvalue counting function and let $c_W(x)$ be the local Weyl coefficient.

**Pointwise Weyl-law improvement conjecture.** There exists a quantifiable constant $\kappa>0$ such that, for every $x\in K_\varepsilon$,

$$
N(\lambda,x)=(2\pi)^{-2}c_W(x)\lambda^2+O_{\mathcal{S},\varepsilon}(\lambda^{1-\kappa}).
$$

This predicts a polynomial improvement over the usual pointwise Weyl-law remainder on the specified surfaces, uniformly away from the poles. The authors state it as an expected consequence of their methods; no resolution is supplied.
full_literal_record.source_name: Ambre Chabert, “Bounds for quasimodes with polynomially narrow bandwidth on surfaces of revolution”, arXiv:2502.00143 (2026).

368214.title: The odd chromatic number conjecture for k-trees

full_literal_record.title: The odd chromatic number conjecture for k-trees
full_literal_record.statement: Let a **k-tree** be a graph obtained from a complete graph on $k+1$ vertices by repeatedly adding a vertex adjacent to all vertices of an existing $k$-clique. An odd coloring of a graph is a vertex coloring in which every vertex has some color appearing an odd number of times in its neighborhood. For a positive integer $k$, let $f(k)$ be the least integer such that every $k$-tree is odd $(k+f(k))$-colorable. **Odd chromatic number conjecture for k-trees.** For every positive integer $k$, every $k$-tree is odd $(k+2)$-colorable. The conjecture asserts that the lower bound $f(k)\geq 2$ is attained for every $k$. It is known for $k=1,2,3$, while the general case remains open; the currently established upper bound is $k+2\left\lfloor\log_2 k\right\rfloor+3$ colors.
full_literal_record.source_name: Masaki Kashima and Kenta Ozeki, “Odd coloring of k-trees”, arXiv:2504.20573 (2025).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.20573
